mainTopic: Mixed-up קרבנות: the end of the משנה, and why our משנה is needed alongside the משניות in תמורה and עבודה זרה
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about a קרבן that got mixed up with other animals. If it was mixed with disqualified animals, or with a different kind of קרבן, all the animals graze until they get a blemish. Then they are sold and new offerings are bought, and in the second case the owner pays any extra cost himself. If it was mixed with fit חולין, the animals are sold to people who need that kind of offering. If it was mixed with the same kind of קרבן, each animal is offered for its owner. Animals mixed with a בכור or מעשר are eaten under the rules of both, and any offerings can get mixed up except a חטאת with an אשם. The גמרא then asks what 'even one in ten thousand' means, and it rereads the משנה: one forbidden animal hidden among many offerings forbids them all. It asks why this is needed when a משנה in תמורה teaches the same rule. Through רב שימי's answer and a few back-and-forth challenges, it shows that each משנה teaches something the other does not. Finally the גמרא raises a new challenge from a משנה in עבודה זרה about יין נסך, and the answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: Mixed with a hybrid, a fatally injured animal, or a caesarean-born animal
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list of disqualified animals. If a קרבן gets mixed up with one of them, all the animals graze until they get a blemish. Then they are sold, and the money buys a new קרבן of the same kind.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a קרבן got mixed up with a כלאים animal, a טריפה, or an animal born by caesarean section, they all graze until they get a blemish. Then they are sold, and he brings a new offering of the same kind, worth as much as the best animal among them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing a list that started earlier, of disqualified animals that a קרבן might get mixed up with. It gives the rule for this whole list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We cannot offer any of the animals, because any one of them might be the disqualified one. We also cannot sell a holy animal while it has no blemish. So we wait until each animal gets a blemish, sell them, and buy a new קרבן worth as much as the most valuable animal, so the הקדש money is fully covered.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal born from two different species (for example, a sheep and a goat)
An animal with a fatal injury or defect
An animal born by caesarean section (literally, 'coming out of the side')
They graze until they get a blemish and become unfit
With the value of the best animal among them

steps.confusionAlert: 'מֵאוֹתוֹ הַמִּין' does not mean the same species of animal. It means the same kind of קרבן (for example, an עולה for an עולה).

phrases.english: With a hybrid animal, or a fatally injured animal, or one born by caesarean section –
they shall graze until they become blemished, and be sold,
and he shall bring, with the value of the best one among them,
an offering of that same kind.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list of disqualified animals from the previous section
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When a קרבן is mixed with disqualified animals, all of them graze until blemished and are sold. A new קרבן of the same kind is bought for the value of the best one.

steps.title: Mixed with unblemished ordinary animals
steps.stepSummary: If a קרבן got mixed up with fit, unblemished חולין animals, the ordinary animals are sold to people who need that same kind of offering, so each animal ends up offered as that kind of קרבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they got mixed up with unblemished ordinary animals, the ordinary animals are sold for the needs of that same kind of offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to a new case: the קרבן got mixed up with ordinary animals that are perfectly fit to be offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here there is no disqualified animal, so no one needs to wait for a blemish. The ordinary animals are sold to people who need that same kind of קרבן, and since we can't tell them apart, each animal is offered as that kind. That way, whichever animal is really the holy one ends up offered as the right kind of קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary animals that are not holy
Unblemished, so fit to be a קרבן
For the needs of that same kind of offering

phrases.english: If they got mixed up with unblemished ordinary animals –
the ordinary animals shall be sold for the needs of that same kind of offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New case: the animals mixed in are fit, not disqualified
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A קרבן mixed with fit חולין: the חולין animals are sold to people who need that kind of offering.

steps.title: Mixed with other קרבנות of the same kind
steps.stepSummary: If two קרבנות of the same kind got mixed up, each animal is simply offered for whoever its owner is.
steps.simpleTranslation: Holy animals mixed with holy animals of the same kind: this one is offered for whoever its owner is, and that one is offered for whoever its owner is.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה turns to a mix-up between קרבנות. In this case they are the same kind of offering.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both animals need exactly the same service. So it doesn't matter that we don't know which one belongs to whom. Each is offered 'for its owner, whoever that is', and both owners fulfill their obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy animals mixed with holy animals
The same kind of offering mixed with its own kind
For the sake of whoever it belongs to

phrases.english: Holy animals mixed with holy animals, the same kind with its own kind –
this one shall be offered for the sake of whoever it belongs to,
and that one shall be offered for the sake of whoever it belongs to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: New case: a קרבן mixed with another קרבן of the same kind
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Same-kind קרבנות that got mixed up are each offered for their unknown owner.

steps.title: Mixed with a different kind of קרבן
steps.stepSummary: If קרבנות of different kinds got mixed up, they graze until blemished and are sold. The owner buys one of each kind, each worth as much as the best animal, and pays the extra from his own money.
steps.simpleTranslation: Holy animals mixed with holy animals of a different kind: they graze until blemished and are sold. He brings an offering of this kind and an offering of that kind, each worth as much as the best one among them, and he covers the extra cost from his own pocket.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives its last case: two different kinds of קרבנות got mixed up, for example an עולה and a שלמים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each kind needs different service, so we cannot offer either animal without risking doing it wrong. We use רעיה, as in step 1. Since we don't know which animal was the more valuable one, each new קרבן must be worth as much as the best animal. The money from the sale won't cover two 'best' animals, so the owner pays the difference himself.

keyTerms.meaning: One kind of offering mixed with a different kind
He will lose (the money)
The extra amount
From his own pocket (literally, 'from his house')

steps.whatToRemember: Four cases: mixed with disqualified animals → רעיה and buy a new one. Mixed with fit חולין → sell to people who need that kind. Same kind of קרבן → offer each for its owner. Different kinds → רעיה, buy two at the top price, and the owner pays the extra.

phrases.english: Holy animals mixed with holy animals, one kind with a different kind –
they shall graze until they become blemished, and be sold,

phrases.aramaic: וְיָבִיא בִּדְמֵי יָפֶה שֶׁבָּהֶן מִמִּין זֶה,
phrases.english: and he shall bring, with the value of the best among them, an offering of this kind,
and, with the value of the best among them, an offering of that kind,
and he loses the extra amount from his own pocket.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The opposite of step 3: here the קרבנות are different kinds, so they cannot be offered
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Different-kind קרבנות that got mixed up go to רעיה. The owner replaces each at the value of the best animal and pays the difference from his own money.

steps.title: Mixed with a firstborn or a tithe animal
steps.stepSummary: If animals got mixed with a בכור or מעשר בהמה, they all graze until they get a blemish, and then they are eaten under the rules of a בכור and a מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: If they got mixed up with a firstborn or with a tithe animal, they graze until they become blemished, and they are eaten like a firstborn and like a tithe animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives one more mixture case: animals mixed with a בכור or a מעשר. They wait until they are blemished and are then eaten with the rules of both.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the earlier cases the blemished animals were sold and the money bought new קרבנות. Here the משנה does not say they are sold. Instead they are eaten, and each animal carries the rules of both a בכור and a מעשר, because we cannot tell which one is which.

keyTerms.meaning: A firstborn male animal, which is holy from birth.
The animal tithe: every tenth animal is set aside as holy.
They graze, meaning they are left out in the pasture.
Until they become blemished and unfit to be offered.

phrases.english: If they were mixed up with a firstborn or with a tithe animal,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the קרבנות the משנה has been talking about in the earlier cases.

phrases.english: they graze until they become blemished,
and they are eaten like a firstborn and like a tithe animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another mixture case to the list in steps 1-4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Animals mixed with a בכור or מעשר graze until blemished and are eaten under the rules of both a בכור and a מעשר.

steps.title: Any offerings can get mixed up except a sin offering and a guilt offering
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that every kind of offering can get mixed up with another, except a חטאת with an אשם.
steps.simpleTranslation: All offerings can become mixed up, except for a sin offering and a guilt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה closes with a general rule: any two kinds of offerings can be confused with each other, except a חטאת and an אשם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that a חטאת and an אשם are not the kind of animals that can get confused for each other. The משנה does not give the reason here. The גמרא explains it later.

keyTerms.meaning: A sin offering.
A guilt offering.
Able to become mixed up so you can't tell them apart.

phrases.english: All offerings can become mixed up,
except for a sin offering and a guilt offering.
phrases.notes: He means a חטאת can't get mixed up with an אשם. The גמרא explains why later.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַכֹּל יְכוֹלִין לְהִתְעָרֵב, חוּץ מִן הַחַטָּאת וְהָאָשָׁם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A general closing rule for all the mixture cases, with one exception.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any offerings can become mixed up, except a חטאת with an אשם.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's mixture cases apply to every kind of offering, with one exception: a חטאת and an אשם never get mixed up with each other.

steps.title: Why does the משנה say 'even'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the word 'even' adds in the משנה's first case about mixtures with forbidden animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What is the meaning of 'even'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and challenges a word in the משנה's opening case: 'even one in ten thousand.' The question sets up the next step, where the גמרא will reread the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said offerings 'mixed into' forbidden animals, like חטאות המתות, must all die. That sounds like one good animal lost among many forbidden ones. In that case it is obvious that they are forbidden, so saying 'even one in ten thousand' seems to add nothing.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה.
What does the word 'even' come to add?

phrases.english: גמרא: What is the meaning of 'even'?
phrases.notes: This refers to the very start of the משנה: 'even one in ten thousand, they all must die.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The משנה is finished, and the גמרא returns to its first clause to question the wording.
steps.kashyaTarget: The word 'even' in the משנה's line 'even one in ten thousand, they all must die.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If one offering got mixed into many forbidden animals, it is obviously forbidden. So 'even one in ten thousand' seems pointless.

steps.title: Read it the other way: one forbidden animal among many offerings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the משנה means a forbidden animal got mixed into many offerings. Even one forbidden animal in ten thousand makes them all have to die.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: all offerings into which sin offerings left to die, or an ox sentenced to stoning, got mixed, even one in ten thousand, they all must die.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by rereading the משנה. The forbidden animal is the one mixed into the offerings, not the other way around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now 'even' makes sense. A single forbidden animal lost among ten thousand good offerings still forbids every one of them, so a majority of good animals does not help. This is a real חידוש, and it is the reason the משנה needed the word.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it is saying, a phrase that introduces a rereading.
Sin offerings that are left to die and cannot be used.
An ox sentenced to be stoned, which nobody may get any benefit from.
One in ten thousand.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
all the offerings into which were mixed
sin offerings left to die or an ox sentenced to stoning,
even one in ten thousand,
they all must die.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about 'even' by rereading the משנה's case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה meant one offering mixed into many forbidden animals, which would make 'even' pointless.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה means one forbidden animal mixed into many offerings. Even one in ten thousand forbids them all, so 'even' teaches that a majority does not cancel it.
steps.whatToRemember: With חטאות המתות or a שור הנסקל, even one forbidden animal hidden among ten thousand offerings forbids all of them, and a majority does not help.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't picture one good animal lost among bad ones. The גמרא reads it the opposite way: one bad animal lost among many good ones still forbids them all.

steps.title: Didn't we already learn this in another משנה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges our משנה. A משנה in תמורה already teaches that animals forbidden for the altar forbid a whole mixture in any amount, such as a רובע and a נרבע.
steps.simpleTranslation: We already learned this once: all animals forbidden for the altar make a mixture forbidden in any amount, such as an animal that lay with a person and an animal that a person lay with!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why our משנה is needed. It seems to repeat a rule we already know from a different משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 8 explained that one forbidden animal mixed into ten thousand forbids them all. But the משנה in תמורה already says forbidden animals forbid a mixture 'in any amount'. So our משנה looks like a repeat.

keyTerms.meaning: We already learned this once (in another משנה)
They forbid in any amount; even a tiny ratio does not cancel them
An animal that actively lay with a person
An animal that a person lay with
For the altar, meaning as a קרבן

phrases.english: We already learned this one time:
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in תמורה (28a).

phrases.english: All animals that are forbidden for the altar
make a mixture forbidden in any amount,
such as an animal that lay with a person, and an animal that a person lay with!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the need for the משנה as step 8 explained it
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה in תמורה already teaches that forbidden animals forbid a mixture in any amount, so our משנה seems to repeat it.

steps.title: רב שימי explains why both משניות are needed
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי reports רב שימי's answer. From תמורה alone we might think the rule applies only to the altar. From our משנה alone we might think it applies only to animals forbidden for benefit. So both are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: I said this teaching before רב שימי, and he told me both are needed. If we had only the משנה in תמורה, I would say the rule applies only to the altar, but not to ordinary use. If we had only our משנה, I would say the rule applies only to animals forbidden for benefit, but not to the animals listed in תמורה. So both are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers the question by showing that each משנה teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in תמורה is about bringing animals on the altar, so it does not tell us that an ordinary person may not use the mixture. Our משנה is about animals that no one may benefit from at all, like a שור הנסקל, so it does not tell us the rule for animals that are only unfit for the altar. Each משנה fills the other's gap.

keyTerms.meaning: And he showed me that both are needed
I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
The Most High, meaning the altar and holy use
An ordinary person, meaning everyday non-holy use
Things that no one may get any benefit from
They are both needed

steps.confusionAlert: 'From there' means the משנה in תמורה, and 'from here' means our משנה in זבחים. Keep the two straight.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
I said this teaching in front of Rav Shimi,
and he explained to me that both are needed:
for if I had it only from there, I would have said:
this applies only to the Most High,
but for an ordinary person, I would say not;
phrases.notes: He means the mixture would not be forbidden for regular, non-holy use.

phrases.english: and if I had it only from here, I would have said:
it is only these that are forbidden for any benefit,
phrases.notes: He means the cases in our משנה, like a חטאת that must die or an ox sentenced to stoning.

phrases.english: but those other animals, I would say not;
so both are needed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: אַמְרִיתַהּ לִשְׁמַעְתֵּיהּ קַמֵּיהּ דְּרַב שִׁימִי, וְאַצְרִיכַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: צריכותא: each source teaches something the other does not
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Each משנה alone would teach only part of the rule: only for the altar, or only for animals forbidden for benefit.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both משניות are needed to teach the full rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the full rule. Animals that are איסורי הנאה forbid a whole mixture even for ordinary use. Animals that are forbidden only for the altar, like a רובע, also forbid a whole mixture, but only for the altar.

steps.title: Our משנה already lists the animals not forbidden for benefit
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back. Our משנה already lists animals that are not forbidden for benefit, like the רובע and נרבע. So what does the משנה in תמורה add?
steps.simpleTranslation: The animals that are not forbidden for benefit, our משנה already taught them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer, this time asking why the משנה in תמורה is needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה itself lists the רובע and נרבע, which are not forbidden for benefit. So the second half of רב שימי's answer seems to fall apart, and the משנה in תמורה looks like the extra one.

keyTerms.meaning: But he already taught it!

phrases.english: The animals that are not forbidden for benefit —
phrases.notes: Our משנה also lists the רובע and נרבע, which you may still benefit from.

phrases.english: he already taught them here!

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּלָאו אִיסּוּרֵי הֲנָאָה נִינְהוּ הָא תְּנָא לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the second half of רב שימי's answer
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the משנה in תמורה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Our משנה already covers animals not forbidden for benefit, so the משנה in תמורה seems to add nothing.

steps.title: Only the משנה in תמורה says 'in any amount'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that our משנה never says how small an amount still forbids the mixture. Only the משנה in תמורה says 'in any amount', and that is what it adds.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does our משנה teach by how much? 'In any amount' is taught there, in תמורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. It shows that the משנה in תמורה adds the exact amount: any amount at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה tells us the animals are forbidden, but it does not clearly say that even one in a huge mixture is enough. The words 'in any amount' appear only in תמורה. So both משניות stay needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Does it teach? (a question that expects the answer 'no')
By how much; in what ratio

steps.whatToRemember: Both משניות are needed. Ours teaches that the mixture is forbidden even for ordinary use. The one in תמורה teaches that any amount at all forbids the mixture.

phrases.english: Does our משנה teach by how much?!
'In any amount' is taught only there.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Points to wording found only in one source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה in תמורה seemed to add nothing new.
steps.terutzMaskana: It adds the words 'in any amount', which our משנה does not say.

steps.title: Then let the משנה in תמורה teach it, and drop ours
steps.stepSummary: If only the משנה in תמורה teaches 'in any amount,' then that משנה should be enough. Why do we need our משנה's clause about mixed-up animals at all?
steps.simpleTranslation: Then let the תנא teach that משנה in תמורה, and he would not need this one here!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is pushing back on the answer from Step 12. If the 'any amount' rule comes only from תמורה, then our משנה's clause seems unnecessary.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 said the משנה in תמורה adds the detail of 'in any amount.' But that makes the תמורה משנה the complete source. So our משנה's case of animals mixed with a רובע or נרבע now looks extra.

keyTerms.meaning: Then let him teach (a challenge: this one source should be enough)
and he would not need
this one (pointing to a specific משנה)

phrases.english: Then let him teach that one, and he would not need this one!
phrases.notes: The first 'that one' is the משנה in תמורה; the second 'this one' is our משנה's clause about the mixed-up animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 12 by turning it around. If תמורה is the full source, our clause seems extra.
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for our משנה's clause about offerings mixed with animals forbidden for the altar
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the תמורה משנה gives the full rule including 'any amount,' it alone is enough. Our משנה adds nothing.

steps.title: Our משנה is needed to teach the remedy
steps.stepSummary: Our משנה is still needed because it teaches the practical fix for such a mixture. The תמורה משנה does not teach that.
steps.simpleTranslation: The remedy was what he needed to teach.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that our משנה teaches something new: what to do with the mixed-up animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תמורה משנה only says the mixture is forbidden. Our משנה adds the fix: the animals graze until they get a blemish. Then they are sold, and the owner uses the money of the best one to bring a new offering of that type. That practical instruction is the reason our clause is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: the remedy / the practical fix
it was needed by him (the תנא needed to teach it)

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה in תמורה teaches the rule ('in any amount'). Our משנה teaches the fix (graze, sell, buy a new offering).

phrases.english: The remedy was what he needed [to teach].
phrases.notes: The remedy is the part of our משנה where the animals graze until blemished, are sold, and new offerings are bought with the money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 13 by pointing to new content found only in our משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Each source has its own unique content: our משנה adds the practical remedy
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our clause seemed to repeat what תמורה already teaches.
steps.terutzMaskana: Our clause is needed to teach the remedy of grazing, selling, and replacing the offerings.

steps.title: For ordinary items, the משנה in עבודה זרה already teaches this
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא now challenges the first clause of our משנה. A משנה in עבודה זרה already teaches that items forbidden for benefit, like יין נסך and עבודה זרה, forbid a mixture in any amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: For an ordinary person, the rule is also taught: 'These are forbidden, and they forbid a mixture in any amount: יין נסך and עבודה זרה!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new challenge. It points to a משנה in עבודה זרה that seems to already teach our משנה's rule about items forbidden for benefit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה said offerings mixed with a חטאת that must die or an ox that must be stoned all become forbidden. That is a rule about things forbidden for any benefit. But the משנה in עבודה זרה already teaches that such items (יין נסך, עבודה זרה) forbid a mixture in any amount, even for ordinary non-holy use. So why is our clause needed? The answer comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: an ordinary person / ordinary non-holy use
forbidden themselves, and they make others forbidden
wine poured as an offering to an idol
idol worship (objects used for it)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two challenges. Steps 13–14 were about animals forbidden only for the altar (רובע, נרבע). This step is about things forbidden for any benefit (חטאת that must die, שור הנסקל).

phrases.english: For an ordinary person, he also taught it:
phrases.notes: This means the rule for everyday, non-holy items, as opposed to the altar.

phrases.english: "And these are forbidden, and they forbid in any amount:
phrases.notes: This is a quote from a משנה in עבודה זרה.
